1        Floating-Point Model
We assume the standard floating-point model [1]: for every elementary operation ◦ ∈ {+, −, ×, /},
                                      fl(a ◦ b) = (a ◦ b)(1 + δ),   |δ| ≤ u,                       (1)
where u is the unit roundoff and δ is the relative roundoff error. Using eq. (1) for numerical analysis
we typicall obtain the product
                                Yn

                                       i=1
where n denotes the number of accumulated roundoff error terms. For numerical analysis, we seek
reliable and sharp bounds for θn .


2        Deterministic Rounding Error Analysis
The deterministic rounding error analysis proposes the following problem-size dependent constant

                                                1 − nu
for nu < 1. Here, n is the number of accumulated error terms [1]. The problem-size dependent
constant is monotonic, that is, γn+1 > γn for u > 0. Performing backward/forward error analysis
using eq. (3) we obtain
                                                     |θn | ≤ γn .                                  (4)
